Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.passkeys

Class PasskeyChainCustomizer

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.passkeys.PasskeyChainCustomizer
All Implemented Interfaces:
LoginChainCustomizer
public class PasskeyChainCustomizer extends Object implements LoginChainCustomizer
Customizes the login/UI chain with the passkeys (WebAuthn).

http.webAuthn(...) adds the filters of the four framework endpoints (the authentication options, the authentication, the registration options and the registration) and this class makes them safe for this server:

  • the options and the sign-in post are public (CSRF stays on: the page script sends the token), as is the script;
  • the registration endpoints (and the account page that drives them) require a session that satisfies the multi-factor policy of its account, see PasskeyRegistrationAuthorizationManager;
  • the framework's DELETE /webauthn/register/{id} is denied, so a passkey can only be removed through DELETE /api/account/passkeys/{id}, which asks for a recent multi-factor sign-in, and its default registration page is turned off;
  • the WebAuthn filter gets the chain's session strategy (new session id on sign-in) and a user service that refuses disabled accounts. That user service is set as the chain's shared UserDetailsService, so it is chain-wide: every configurer of the login chain that reads the shared object gets the account-status check;
  • a passkey that completes a second-factor step is refused while the user's second factor is locked, see PasskeySecondFactorLockoutFilter. That filter is added before BasicAuthenticationFilter, the position the WebAuthn configurer gives its authentication filter later, when the chain is built; being added first, it runs first.
